## Data import, parsing & cleaning

We start by loading the required libraries.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(ismev)
```

Next, we fetch data from our chosen river gauging station, *Don at Parkhill* in Scotland. For 10 years of 15-minute interval data, we are fetching over 350,000 records. To minimise the chances of a 504 Gateway Timeout, we will fetch the data in 1-year blocks and save it to our local disk so future runs do not have to re-download the data.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Extend R's default HTTP timeout limit to 300 seconds
options(timeout = 300)

cache_file <- "river_don_parkhill_flow.rds"

if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
  # Load from local cache if file already exists
  river_data <- readRDS(cache_file)
  
} else {
  # If no local cache exists, fetch from SEPA in 1-year chunks
  start_years <- seq(2016, 2025, by = 1)
  
  fetch_chunk <- function(yr) {
    from_date <- paste0(yr, "-08-31T00:00:00")
    to_date   <- paste0(yr + 1, "-08-31T00:00:00")
    
    url <- paste0(
      "https://timeseries.sepa.org.uk/KiWIS/KiWIS?",
      "service=kisters&type=queryServices&datasource=0&",
      "request=getTimeseriesValues&ts_path=1/234292/Q/15m.Cmd&",
      "from=", from_date, "&to=", to_date, "&",
      "metadata=true&returnfields=Timestamp,Value,Quality%20Code&format=csv"
    )
    
    read_delim(
      url, 
      delim = ";", 
      comment = "#",
      col_names = c("Timestamp", "Discharge", "QualityCode"),
      show_col_types = FALSE
    )
  }
  
  river_data <- map_dfr(start_years, fetch_chunk) %>%
    mutate(Timestamp = as.POSIXct(Timestamp, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Discharge)) %>%
    distinct(Timestamp, .keep_all = TRUE)
  
  # Save to local file so future runs don't need to use the API
  saveRDS(river_data, cache_file)
}
```

Shifting our attention to the `QualityCode` column, let us assess the data segmented by quality code.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Create the quality code table from SEPA guidance
quality_code_table <- tibble(
  `Code number` = c(50, 100, 140, 150, 200, 254),
  `Code name` = c(
    "Good", 
    "Estimated", 
    "Provisional", 
    "Suspect", 
    "Unchecked<br>(imported from legacy database)", 
    "Unchecked"
  ),
  `Abbreviated code name` = c("G", "E", "Prov", "S", "V", "U")
)

# Generate table
quality_code_table %>%
  kable(
    format = "html", 
    escape = FALSE, 
    caption = "Table 1 — quality codes",
    align = c("c", "l", "c") # c = center, l = left
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("bordered", "striped", "hover"), 
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "left"
  )
```

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Segment data by QualityCode split
quality_summary <- river_data %>%
  count(QualityCode) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = sprintf("%.2f%%", (n / sum(n)) * 100)
  )

print(quality_summary)
```

We observe that 95.89% of our data is "Good" by SEPA's quality control standards.

Below is the statistical summary of the 15-minute flow discharge ($m^3/s$) for the River Don at Parkhill across the 10-year period:

```{r, echo=TRUE}
summary(river_data$Discharge)
```

## River Hydrograph

```{r, echo=TRUE}
ggplot(river_data, aes(x = Timestamp, y = Discharge)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Hydrograph: Don at Parkhill (15-min Interval)",
    subtitle = "August 2016 – August 2026",
    x = "Date",
    y = expression("Discharge ("*m^3*"/s)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Exploratory Analysis

## Time variables

We add three time variables used throughout this section: the month, the season, and the water year. A water year runs from September to August and is labelled by the year it ends in, which keeps each winter's high flows together in the same year.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
river_data <- river_data %>%
  mutate(
    month      = month(Timestamp, label = TRUE),
    water_year = if_else(month(Timestamp) >= 9, year(Timestamp) + 1, year(Timestamp)),
    season     = case_when(
      month(Timestamp) %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
      month(Timestamp) %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring",
      month(Timestamp) %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer",
      TRUE                              ~ "Autumn"
    ),
    season = factor(season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Autumn"))
  )
```

## Long-term pattern

Adding the monthly mean and the overall mean to the hydrograph shows the contrast between the typical flow, which moves smoothly with the seasons, and the short peaks that rise far above it.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
monthly_mean <- river_data %>%
  group_by(month_start = floor_date(Timestamp, "month")) %>%
  summarise(Discharge = mean(Discharge))

ggplot(river_data, aes(x = Timestamp, y = Discharge)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = monthly_mean, aes(x = month_start), color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(river_data$Discharge), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Hydrograph with monthly and overall mean",
    subtitle = "Black line: monthly mean. Red dashed line: overall mean.",
    x = "Date",
    y = expression("Discharge ("*m^3*"/s)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r, echo=TRUE}
river_data %>%
  summarise(
    `Mean`               = mean(Discharge),

    `25th percentile`    = quantile(Discharge, 0.25),

  ) %>%

    bootstrap_options = c("bordered", "striped", "hover"),
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "left"
  )
```

Flow is strongly right-skewed: most of the time the river is low, with occasional very high peaks. A log scale makes the shape easier to see.

```{r, echo=TRUE}

             linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +

    title = "Distribution of 15-minute discharge",

```


## Shape of an individual event

Zooming in on the 30 days either side of the largest recorded flow shows the shape of individual hydrograph peaks: a fast rise followed by a slower fall.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
biggest <- river_data$Timestamp[which.max(river_data$Discharge)]

river_data %>%
  filter(Timestamp >= biggest - 30 * 24 * 3600,
         Timestamp <= biggest + 30 * 24 * 3600) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Timestamp, y = Discharge)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Hydrograph around the largest recorded flow",
    subtitle = paste("Peak on", format(biggest, "%d %B %Y")),
    x = "Date",
    y = expression("Discharge ("*m^3*"/s)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Threshold

## 3-5 per year method

```{r}
# Thresholds to try: 0, 1, 2, ... up to the maximum flow
thresholds <- 0:max(river_data$Discharge)

# Peaks per year for each threshold
peaks_per_year <- sapply(thresholds, function(u) {
  above <- river_data$Discharge > u
  sum(above & !lag(above, default = FALSE))
}) / n_distinct(river_data$water_year)

# Thresholds giving 3 to 5 peaks per year
thresholds[peaks_per_year >= 3 & peaks_per_year <= 5]

# Plot
ggplot(tibble(thresholds, peaks_per_year), aes(x = thresholds, y = peaks_per_year)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(3, 5), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = expression("Threshold ("*m^3*"/s)"), y = "Peaks per year") +
  theme_minimal()
```


## Percentile method

```{r}
# Threshold: the 95th percentile of flow
u95 <- quantile(river_data$Discharge, 0.95)
u95

# Peaks: the highest reading in each separate period above the threshold
peaks_95 <- river_data %>%
  mutate(above = Discharge > u95,
         start = above & !lag(above, default = FALSE),   # TRUE when the flow first goes above the threshold
         run   = cumsum(start)) %>%                       # numbers each period above the threshold
  filter(above) %>%
  group_by(run) %>%
  slice_max(Discharge, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

# Number of peaks, and average peaks per year
nrow(peaks_95)
nrow(peaks_95) / n_distinct(river_data$water_year)

# Plot
ggplot(river_data, aes(x = Timestamp, y = Discharge)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = u95, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_point(data = peaks_95, color = "red", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Peaks above the 95th percentile threshold",
    x = "Date",
    y = expression("Discharge ("*m^3*"/s)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# Count the peaks above a given percentile threshold
count_peaks <- function(p) {
  u <- quantile(river_data$Discharge, p)
  river_data %>%
    mutate(above = Discharge > u,
           start = above & !lag(above, default = FALSE)) %>%
    summarise(n = sum(start)) %>%
    pull(n)
}

# Try a range of percentiles
threshold_table <- tibble(percentile = c(0.90, 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98, 0.99, 0.995)) %>%
  mutate(
    threshold      = quantile(river_data$Discharge, percentile),
    peaks          = sapply(percentile, count_peaks),
    peaks_per_year = peaks / n_distinct(river_data$water_year)
  )

threshold_table

# Plot
ggplot(threshold_table, aes(x = percentile * 100, y = peaks_per_year)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(3, 5), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Peaks per year for different percentile thresholds",
    subtitle = "Red dashed lines: the standard target of 3 to 5 peaks per year",
    x = "Percentile used as threshold",
    y = "Peaks per year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Independent peaks

We apply the Robson and Reed (1999) independence rules from the lecture:

1. Two adjacent peaks must be at least three times the average time to rise apart. The time to rise is the time between a trough and its peak, averaged over at least five clean peaks above the threshold.
2. The flow at the trough between two adjacent peaks must be at least two-thirds lower than the first peak, i.e. below one third of it.

Assumptions:
- a clean peak means no other candidate peak in the previous 7 days;
- the trough is where the rise starts (within 5% of the week’s lowest flow).

If two peaks fail either rule, they belong to the same event and only the larger peak is kept.

```{r}
q <- river_data$Discharge
t <- river_data$Timestamp

independent_peaks <- function(u) {

  # Step 1: candidate peaks - the highest reading in each period above the threshold
  candidates <- river_data %>%
    mutate(row   = row_number(),
           above = Discharge > u,
           run   = cumsum(above & !lag(above, default = FALSE))) %>%
    filter(above) %>%
    group_by(run) %>%
    slice_max(Discharge, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    pull(row)

  # Step 2: average time to rise, calculated using at least five clean peaks exceeding the threshold
  # A clean peak has no other candidate peak in the 7 days before it
  days_since_last <- as.numeric(difftime(t[candidates], lag(t[candidates]), units = "days"))
  clean <- candidates[is.na(days_since_last) | days_since_last > 7]
  if (length(clean) < 5) stop("Fewer than five clean peaks - lower the threshold")

  # Time to rise = duration between a trough and its corresponding peak
  # Trough = last point before the peak still within 5% of the rise above the lowest flow in the previous 7 days
  rise_hours <- sapply(clean, function(p) {
    window <- which(t >= t[p] - 7 * 24 * 3600 & t <= t[p])
    low    <- min(q[window])
    trough <- max(window[q[window] <= low + 0.05 * (q[p] - low)])
    as.numeric(difftime(t[p], t[trough], units = "hours"))
  })

  min_gap_hours <- 3 * mean(rise_hours)

  # Step 3: check each pair of adjacent peaks against both rules
  kept <- candidates[1]
  for (p in candidates[-1]) {
    last   <- kept[length(kept)]                                  # the first peak of the pair
    gap    <- as.numeric(difftime(t[p], t[last], units = "hours"))
    trough <- min(q[last:p])                                      # discharge at the trough between them

    # Rule 1: at least three times the average time to rise apart
    # Rule 2: trough at least two-thirds lower than the first peak
    if (gap >= min_gap_hours & trough <= q[last] / 3) {
      kept <- c(kept, p)                 # independent: a new event
    } else if (q[p] > q[last]) {
      kept[length(kept)] <- p            # same event: keep the larger peak
    }
  }

  cat("Candidate peaks:", length(candidates), "\n")
  cat("Clean peaks used for time to rise:", length(clean), "\n")
  cat("Average time to rise (hours):", round(mean(rise_hours), 1), "\n")
  cat("Independent peaks:", length(kept), "\n")

  river_data[kept, ]
}
```

## Rechecking the threshold

Removing dependent peaks lowers the number of peaks per year, so we recheck which thresholds give 3 to 5 independent peaks per year.

```{r}
check <- tibble(threshold = seq(50, 200, by = 10)) %>%
  mutate(peaks_per_year = sapply(threshold, function(u) nrow(independent_peaks(u))) /
                          n_distinct(river_data$water_year))
check
```

Approx 65 for threshold?

```{r}
u <- 65   # change to your final threshold
peaks <- independent_peaks(u)

# Row number of each peak, and of the peak before it
peak_rows <- match(peaks$Timestamp, t)
previous  <- c(1, head(peak_rows, -1))

# Start of each rise: same definition as the trough in the time to rise,
# searching back up to 7 days but never past the previous peak
start_rows <- mapply(function(p, prev) {
  window <- which(t >= max(t[p] - 7 * 24 * 3600, t[prev]) & t <= t[p])
  low    <- min(q[window])
  max(window[q[window] <= low + 0.05 * (q[p] - low)])
}, peak_rows, previous)

# The two quantities SEPA asked for
peaks <- peaks %>%
  mutate(
    start_time     = t[start_rows],
    max_flow       = Discharge,
    time_to_peak_h = as.numeric(difftime(Timestamp, start_time, units = "hours"))
  )

peaks %>% select(start_time, Timestamp, max_flow, time_to_peak_h)
summary(peaks$time_to_peak_h)
```

```{r}
# Max flow
ggplot(peaks, aes(x = max_flow)) +

# Time to peak

```

```{r}
cor.test(peaks$time_to_peak_h, peaks$max_flow, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
```

```{r}
results <- tibble()

for (u in c(55, 60, 65, 70, 75)) {
  peaks <- independent_peaks(u)

  # Start of each rise and time to peak (same code as before)
  peak_rows <- match(peaks$Timestamp, t)
  previous  <- c(1, head(peak_rows, -1))
  start_rows <- mapply(function(p, prev) {
    window <- which(t >= max(t[p] - 7 * 24 * 3600, t[prev]) & t <= t[p])
    low    <- min(q[window])
    max(window[q[window] <= low + 0.05 * (q[p] - low)])
  }, peak_rows, previous)
  time_to_peak_h <- as.numeric(difftime(peaks$Timestamp, t[start_rows], units = "hours"))

  # One row of results for this threshold
  results <- bind_rows(results, tibble(
    threshold             = u,
    events                = nrow(peaks),
    events_per_year       = nrow(peaks) / n_distinct(river_data$water_year),
    median_max_flow       = median(peaks$Discharge),
    median_time_to_peak_h = median(time_to_peak_h),
    spearman_rho          = cor(peaks$Discharge, time_to_peak_h, method = "spearman")
  ))
}

results
```
